import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# Paths
input_dir = "./input"
submission_dir = "./submission"


def clip_probs(probs):
    return np.clip(probs, 1e-15, 1 - 1e-15)


def calculate_logloss(y_true_idx, y_prob, eps=1e-15):
    """Calculate multi-class logarithmic loss."""
    # y_prob shape: (N_samples, N_classes)
    # y_true_idx: (N_samples,)
    # Ensure y_prob sums to 1 for proper logging (rescaling as per instructions)
    y_prob = clip_probs(y_prob)

    # Rescale row-wise to sum to 1 (standard practice, instructions imply this happens before scoring)
    y_prob = np.array([p / np.sum(p) for p in y_prob])

    y_prob = clip_probs(y_prob)

    loss = -np.mean(np.sum(y_true_idx * np.log(y_prob), axis=1))
    return float(loss)


# Load sample submission to get correct header and class ordering
sample_sub_path = f"{input_dir}/sample_submission.csv"
sample_df = pd.read_csv(sample_sub_path)
species_cols = sample_df.columns[1:]  # Exclude 'id'
num_species = len(species_cols)

# Load Training Data
train_path = f"{input_dir}/train.csv"
train_df = pd.read_csv(train_path)

# Extract Features
feature_cols = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in ["id", "species"]]
# Ensure consistent column order for test set later
if len(feature_cols) == 0:
    raise ValueError("No feature columns found in train data.")

# Prepare Labels
y_train_labels = train_df["species"].tolist()
X_train_raw = train_df[feature_cols].values.astype("float32")

# Create label encoder based on sample submission order
train_label_map = {label: i for i, label in enumerate(species_cols)}
y_train_encoded = train_df["species"].map(train_label_map).values
classes_count = len(train_label_map.values())

# Split for Hold-out Validation (70/30 to maximize training data)
X_train_fit, X_val, y_train_enc, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train_raw, y_train_encoded, test_size=0.30, random_state=42, stratify=y_train_enc
)

# Train Model (Lightning Bolt / LR with L2 penalty is good for tabular, avoiding deep trees for small dataset safety)
# Using LogisticRegression with L2 regularization to prevent overfitting on small classes
model = LogisticRegression(
    solver="lbfgs",
    max_iter=1000,
    C=10.0,  # Higher C for strong regularization needed for small classes
    n_jobs=-1,
    random_state=42,
)

# Fit on Training Set Only (Val excluded from fit)
model.fit(X_train_fit, y_train_enc)

# Evaluate on Validation Set (Hold-out)
y_val_pred = model.predict_proba(X_val)
val_metric = calculate_logloss(y_val, y_val_pred)

print(f"Hold-out Validation LogLoss: {val_metric}")

# Load and Prepare Test Data
test_path = f"{input_dir}/test.csv"
test_df = pd.read_csv(test_path)
X_test = test_df[feature_cols].values.astype("float32")

# Generate Predictions on Test Set
test_probs = model.predict_proba(X_test)

# Ensure probabilities sum to 1 for robustness
test_probs = np.array([p / np.sum(p) for p in test_probs])
# Clip to avoid log domain errors (as per instructions)
test_probs = clip_probs(test_probs)

# Construct Submission DataFrame
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["id"] + list(species_cols))
submission_df = submission_df.merge(
    pd.DataFrame({"id": test_df["id"]}), on="id", how="outer"
)
# Add prediction columns
for col in species_cols:
    index = species_cols.index(col)
    submission_df[col] = test_probs[:, index]

# Save to specific location
output_path = f"{submission_dir}/submission.csv"
submission_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
